Apple Podcasts is my go-to podcast app, but I've long had a major problem with its core 'Up Next' queue feature. I'm happy to say iOS 27.2 brings the fix.

iOS 27.2 splits Apple Podcasts' 'Up Next' queue into two parts: New Episodes and Keep Listening

There's a lot to love about Apple Podcasts. Transcripts and auto-generated chapters are two killer features that make this app my go-to. I also love all the recent video-related upgrades.

But for years, Apple Podcasts' core 'Up Next' queue has made me want to switch to another app.

I've written before about why the 'Up Next' feature feels broken. In short:

  • It makes it hard to see clearly what's available to listen to
  • Episodes can easily disappear, even if you've only half-listened to them

But I'm excited to say iOS 27.2 finally brings a long-overdue fix to 'Up Next.' It does this by splitting it into two separate sections:

  • New Episodes
  • Keep Listening

At the very top of the app is 'New Episodes,' which looks and works much like 'Up Next' used to. Just as the name suggests, though, it only shows the latest episodes of every show you follow.

Right beneath it is 'Keep Listening,' acting as a central hub for accessing all episodes you've started but haven't finished.

Together, these two sections solve all of my biggest issues with the 'Up Next' queue.

You can easily see at a glance what's new, and I'll never lose track of episodes again, because anything I've already started listening to will be in 'Keep Listening.' I have a few minor nitpicks, but these changes alone have addressed my main problems with 'Up Next.'

If you haven't tried Apple Podcasts in a while, iOS 27.2 is a great time to give it another chance.

Do you use Apple Music or another podcast app? Let us know in the comments.
